content.text:
Yes - and it already did on your machine.

That comment means Cursor can **rewrite** `~/.cursor/.gitignore` (your “managed block”) when it updates user/global Cursor config. In your setup `~/.cursor` is a symlink into this repo, so that rewrite shows up as a dirty tracked file.

Evidence right now:

- **Committed version** still has your explanatory comments.
- **Working tree** (rewritten today ~16:39) is only:

```
*
!.gitignore
!rules/
!rules/**
```

So Cursor kept the same ignore policy, but dropped the comments. The patterns themselves are what Cursor wants for “track `rules/` only.”

That is why root `.gitignore` also allowlists `.cursor/rules/` - even if Cursor nukes or reshapes `.cursor/.gitignore`, the repo-level policy still keeps chats, extensions, skills, etc. out of git.
